A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DINO-SLAM, with matching methods and benchmark experiments despite substantial revision. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Both PDFs end with references; neither contains an appendix section.

before.justification: V1 reports original tracking, reconstruction and rendering results on Replica, ScanNet and TUM, plus component ablations and resource measurements in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, feature ablations, depth-noise experiments and computational measurements in Tables 1–8.

M1.justification: V1 specifies DINO ViT-small, whereas v2 specifies DINOv2 ViT-small. V2 also extends the framework to GauS-SLAM's 2D Gaussian surfels and adopts that system for its principal GS variant, replacing the earlier 3D-Gaussian implementation. These change important model components; the underlying attention-based fusion remains substantially unchanged under the SSE/EDINO to SGE/geoDINO renaming.

E1.justification: The eight Replica scenes, six ScanNet sequences and three TUM sequences remain the benchmark coverage. V2 adds a distinct corrupted-depth input scenario on Replica office1 in Table 4. Adding 2D-surface representations changes the evaluated models, not the underlying task coverage.

E2.justification: The actual comparator sets expand substantially. V2's main Replica comparison adds HS-SLAM, Mamba-SLAM, SNH-SLAM, QQ-SLAM and SNI-SLAM, plus numerous GS methods including GauS-SLAM, SEGS-SLAM and VSS-SLAM. SNI-SLAM previously appeared only in the generality study. Gaussian-SLAM is removed from the ScanNet and TUM comparisons while remaining in Replica.

E3.justification: Standard benchmark scene counts and metrics remain unchanged. The GS component study moves from ScanNet to Replica with GauS-SLAM, and new experiments specify Gaussian depth noise with mean 0 and standard deviation 0.1 and stage-level profiling. Reported hardware changes from A100 to RTX 3090Ti; this does not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a DINO-plus-depth concatenation control, extends the generality study to GauS-SLAM, tests depth-noise robustness, and provides detailed computational overhead and memory analyses. The earlier GS component study is replaced by a Replica study, and its global bundle-adjustment ablation is removed. These substantially revise the evidence about mechanism, robustness and computational cost.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both mainly report individual sequence results and averages across scenes. The new Gaussian noise parameters specify an input corruption, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Numerous results change or are added. Between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 3, reported Replica NeRF RMSE changes from 0.51 to 0.49 cm and SplaTAM PSNR from 33.97 to 34.11 dB. The replaced GS variant reports Replica PSNR of 41.42 rather than 39.12 dB, and TUM RMSE of 1.42 rather than 1.36 cm. Changed backbones prevent treating these as controlled inter-version gains. V2 also adds baseline, noise-test and computational results.

T1.justification: The attention, volume-rendering, Gaussian projection/blending and feature-loss formulations retain their substance. Renamed variables, regrouped equations and explicit ray-batch notation clarify presentation without introducing a substantive derivation. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a DINO-informed design applicable to implicit and explicit RGB-D SLAM. V2 makes overcoming DINO's missing geometry awareness the explicit abstract-level rationale, replacing the broader hierarchy and structural-relationship framing. It also expands the stated compatibility from 3D Gaussians to include 2D Gaussian surfels.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new concatenation control as evidence that simply adding depth is insufficient, acknowledges vulnerability to depth noise while claiming partial robustness, and explicitly discusses the accuracy-versus-speed tradeoff against ESLAM. Its TUM discussion qualifies superiority as an average result rather than success on every sequence. The earlier interpretation supporting global bundle adjustment is removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies that the feature backbone is frozen, SGE is optimized online, and NeRF keyframes use k=4. It changes the reported GPU and adds a project-page link and computational breakdown. Loss weights, tri-plane resolutions and GS keyframe thresholds are retained. The PDFs alone do not establish code availability through the new link.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated discussion of DINO-informed neural representations and prior DINO-based semantic and dynamic SLAM, including SNI-SLAM, LOSS-SLAM and D3 FlowSLAM. It replaces v1's broad assertion that existing systems overlook DINO with a distinction centered on geometry-aware enhancement. Related work also expands substantially to newer implicit, Gaussian and feed-forward systems.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, research positioning and encoder explanation are extensively rewritten. SSE/EDINO become SGE/geoDINO throughout, and ablations move ahead of the state-of-the-art comparisons to organize the experimental narrative around generality and geometry awareness. Author affiliations and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned with new qualitative panels and a performance plot; the combined pipeline diagram becomes separate NeRF and GS figures. The qualitative comparison is revised, benchmark tables are expanded and reorganized, and new depth-noise and computational-breakdown tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the justification of the contribution: it acknowledges earlier DINO-based SLAM, tests geometry-aware fusion against simple depth concatenation, and evaluates stronger comparators. The depth-noise experiment and computational breakdown make robustness and cost more assessable than in v1. The removed bundle-adjustment ablation and continuing absence of run-level uncertainty limit validation, and the changed GS backbone prevents attributing inter-version score differences solely to the encoder. Nevertheless, the clearer novelty positioning and better controlled evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
